stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the puck (or use the $x_0$ slider on the left) to set the starting position, use the $v$ slider on the right to set velocity, then press GO. Try at least two different velocities and change $x_0$ to see how the position-vs-time line reacts.
stages.concept: Uniform rectilinear motion: $x(t) = x_0 + v \cdot t$. The graph of $x$ versus $t$ is a straight line — slope $= v$, y-intercept $= x_0$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit all three rendezvous points. Each $(x^{*}, t^{*})$ demands the puck be at $x^{*}$ exactly when $t^{*}$ elapses. The dashed preview line shows the trajectory your current $v$ will draw — line it up so it passes through every dot.
stages.concept: Solve for $v$ from the rendezvous condition: $x^{*} = x_0 + v \cdot t^{*} \;\Rightarrow\; v = \dfrac{x^{*} - x_0}{t^{*}}$. Positive $v$ moves right, negative $v$ moves left.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No graph, no preview line. Read each target's $(x^{*}, t^{*})$ from the labels, compute $v = (x^{*} - x_0) / t^{*}$ on paper, dial it in and press GO. You have limited shots — commit only when your calculation is done.
stages.concept: Beware the sign: if $x^{*} < x_0$ the puck must move backward, so $v < 0$. Check the units — $v$ is in m/s, not m.

labels.tip1: drag the puck, change v, then GO — watch the graph draw a straight line
labels.tip2: pick v so the dashed line passes through every dot, then GO
labels.tip3: compute v = (x* − x₀) / t* on paper, then GO — no preview, no retries
labels.peek_tip_formula: Uniform motion: v = (x* − x₀) / t*. Read the coordinates, plug in, done.
labels.peek_tip_sign: Check the sign of x* − x₀. If the target is behind the puck, v must be negative.
labels.peek_tip_bounds: v ranges from −10 to +10 m/s. If your calculation lands outside, re-check t* or the arithmetic.

1.1: Drag the puck along the track to set x₀, then move the v slider on the right.
1.2: Press GO to release the puck. Watch how the graph draws a straight line whose slope is v.
1.3: Try v = 0 first (the puck stays put), then a positive v (moves right), then a negative v (retour — moves left).

2.1: The dashed teal line previews where the puck will be at each instant. Aim it through every dot.
2.2: Each dot's t (horizontal) tells you WHEN to be there; its x (vertical) tells you WHERE.
2.3: Solve v = (x* − x₀) / t* for one target, dial that v in, GO. Repeat for each target — you can adjust v between runs.

3.1: Read a target's (x*, t*). Take a moment to compute v = (x* − x₀) / t* on paper.
3.2: Sign matters. x* < x₀ ⇒ v < 0. x* > x₀ ⇒ v > 0. x* = x₀ ⇒ v = 0.
3.3: You have 3 shots for 3 targets — one calculation per target. Commit only when your paper math is done.
